# Temple Scroll Column 4 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 4 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 4:3 — "kevasim benei shanah" — yearling lambs phrasing

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "he-lambs sons-of-a-year" | Literal construct chain preserving ben as "son of" |
| LOGOS | "male lambs a year old" | Standard formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "one-year-old male lambs" | Natural English word order |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "male lambs a year old." This preserves the biblical register while being intelligible. EMET's "sons-of-a-year" is too opaque; PNEUMA's reordering is acceptable but less traditional.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 4:4 — "chattat" — sin offering vs. purification offering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a-sin-offering" | Traditional rendering with hyphenation |
| LOGOS | "a sin offering" | Traditional rendering, standard syntax |
| PNEUMA | "a purification offering" | Follows Milgrom's scholarship on chattat as purification |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "a sin offering." Per project conventions established in Leviticus, chattat is rendered "sin offering" throughout. Consistency across the project takes precedence over PNEUMA's scholarly preference.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Project convention.

---

## 4:5 — "lekhapper" — atonement rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "to-make-atonement for-you" | Literal with hyphenated preposition |
| LOGOS | "to make atonement on your behalf" | Formal rendering with expanded prepositional phrase |
| PNEUMA | "to purify you from sin" | Dynamic rendering interpreting kipper as purification |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "to make atonement on your behalf." "Atonement" (kipper) is the standard biblical English term and must be preserved. PNEUMA's "purify from sin" is interpretive.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 4:7 — grain offering measurements — ephah vs. modern equivalents

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "three-tenths for-the-bull and-two-tenths for-the-ram" | Bare fractions, no unit specified |
| LOGOS | "three-tenths of an ephah for each bull and two-tenths for the ram" | Supplies "ephah" as the implied unit |
| PNEUMA | "six quarts for each bull and four quarts for the ram" | Converts to modern measurements |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering with "ephah." The ancient unit should be named, as the text implies it. PNEUMA's modern conversions are approximate and remove the text from its cultural context. EMET's omission of the unit is too terse.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 4:12 — "sheaf of the wave offering" — omer terminology

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-sheaf of-the-wave-offering" | Hyphenated construct chain |
| LOGOS | "the sheaf of the wave offering" | Standard formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "the bundle of grain as a wave offering" | "Bundle" for 'omer; explanatory "grain" added |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "the sheaf of the wave offering." "Sheaf" ('omer) is the established translation. PNEUMA's "bundle of grain" is unnecessarily informal.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

*Total disagreements: 5*
*Resolution: LOGOS 5, EMET 0, PNEUMA 0, Compromise 0*
